trial_name.text: ATHOS-3 (Angiotensin II for the Treatment of High-Output Shock; study LJ501-CRH01)

citations.quote: The Angiotensin II for the Treatment of High-Output Shock (ATHOS-3) trial was a double-blind study in which 321 adults with septic or other distributive shock who remained hypotensive despite fluid and vasopressor therapy were randomized 1:1 to GIAPREZA or placebo.
The applicant conducted one double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized, multicenter trial (LJ501-CRH01, “ATHOS-3”) under a SPA agreement.

design.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized (1:1) multicenter trial conducted under a special protocol assessment (SPA), with study drug titrated to a target mean arterial pressure (MAP).

citations.quote: The Angiotensin II for the Treatment of High-Output Shock (ATHOS-3) trial was a double-blind study in which 321 adults with septic or other distributive shock who remained hypotensive despite fluid and vasopressor therapy were randomized 1:1 to GIAPREZA or placebo.
The applicant conducted one double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized, multicenter trial (LJ501-CRH01, “ATHOS-3”) under a SPA agreement.

population.text: Adults with septic or other distributive (catechol-resistant) shock who remained hypotensive (MAP 55 to 70 mmHg) despite fluid and vasopressor therapy; 91% had septic shock.

citations.quote: The Angiotensin II for the Treatment of High-Output Shock (ATHOS-3) trial was a double-blind study in which 321 adults with septic or other distributive shock who remained hypotensive despite fluid and vasopressor therapy were randomized 1:1 to GIAPREZA or placebo.
91% of subjects had septic shock; the remaining subjects had other forms of distributive shock such as neurogenic shock.

Patients were hospitalized adults (\geq 18 years of age) with “catechol resistant hypotension” (CRH) receiving norepinephrine equivalent dose (NED) of > 0.2 mcg/kg/min (based on the sum of the NED scores for each vasopressor given to the patient) and a MAP of 55 to 70 mmHg for 6 to 48 hours prior to randomization

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: percentage of subjects achieving a MAP ≥ 75 mmHg or a ≥ 10 mmHg increase in MAP without an increase in baseline vasopressor therapy at 3 hours.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was the percentage of subjects who achieved either a MAP \ge 75 mmHg or a \ge 10 mmHg increase in MAP without an increase in baseline vasopressor therapy at 3 hours.

n.text: 321 patients in the mITT population (163 GIAPREZA, 158 placebo)

citations.quote: The mITT population included 163 and 158 patients in the angiotensin II and placebo arm, respectively.

The Angiotensin II for the Treatment of High-Output Shock (ATHOS-3) trial was a double-blind study in which 321 adults with septic or other distributive shock who remained hypotensive despite fluid and vasopressor therapy were randomized 1:1 to GIAPREZA or placebo.

result.text: Primary endpoint achieved by 70% (114/163) on GIAPREZA vs 23% (37/158) on placebo (OR=7.95, 95% CI 4.76, 13.3, p=2.54E-15). Day-28 mortality 46% vs 54% (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.57–1.07), not statistically significant.

citations.quote: Results for the primary endpoint of MAP response rate strongly favored angiotensin II, with 114 (70%) vs. 37 (23%) responders in the angiotensin II and placebo arm, respectively (OR=7.95, 95% CI, 4.76, 13.3, p=2.54E-15).
The mITT population included 163 and 158 patients in the angiotensin II and placebo arm, respectively.
Mortality through Day 28 was 46% on GIAPREZA and 54% on placebo (hazard ratio 0.78; 95% confidence interval 0.57 – 1.07).

indication.text: GIAPREZA increases blood pressure in adults with septic or other distributive shock.

citations.quote: GIAPREZA increases blood pressure in adults with septic or other distributive shock.

target_moa.text: Angiotensin II is a naturally occurring peptide hormone of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system that raises blood pressure by vasoconstriction and increased aldosterone release, acting via the G-protein-coupled angiotensin II receptor type 1 on vascular smooth muscle cells.

citations.quote: Angiotensin II is a naturally occurring peptide hormone of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) that causes vasoconstriction and an increase in blood pressure.

Angiotensin II raises blood pressure by vasoconstriction and increased aldosterone release. Direct action of angiotensin II on the vessel wall is mediated by binding to the G-protein-coupled angiotensin II receptor type 1 on vascular smooth muscle cells, which stimulates Ca^{2+}/calmodulin-dependent phosphorylation of myosin and causes smooth muscle contraction.

modality.text: Peptide (synthetic human angiotensin II, an 8-amino-acid peptide hormone)

citations.quote: GIAPREZA is a sterile, aqueous solution of synthetic human angiotensin II for intravenous administration by infusion.
The chemical name of the synthetic angiotensin II acetate is L-Aspartyl-L-arginyl-L-valyl-L-tyrosyl-L-isoleucyl-L-histidyl-L-prolyl-L-phenylalanine, acetate salt.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were thromboembolic events. Higher incidence of arterial and venous thrombotic/thromboembolic events vs placebo (13% vs 5%), including deep vein thrombosis (4.3% vs 0.0%). Other AEs: thrombocytopenia (9.8% vs 7.0%), tachycardia (8.6% vs 5.7%), fungal infection (6.1% vs 1.3%).

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions reported in greater than 10% in GIAPREZA treated patients were thromboembolic events. (6.1)
There was a higher incidence of arterial and venous thrombotic and thromboembolic events in patients who received GIAPREZA compared to placebo-treated patients in the ATHOS-3 study (13% vs. 5%).

summary.text: The NDA was submitted 6/29/2017 as a new molecular entity and granted Priority Review (PDUFA goal 2/28/2018). Approval was a first-cycle, full (traditional) approval based on the single adequate and well-controlled trial ATHOS-3, conducted under a special protocol assessment. No advisory committee was convened; pediatric studies were deferred as required postmarketing studies under PREA.
